newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Alestra says has 72 pct LD suscriptions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Alestra says has 72 pct LD suscriptions.

text.p: The AT&T-backed Mexican telecommunications company, Alestra, said on Thursday that it had received 72 percent of the presubscription ballots returned to date for long-distance telephone services in the north city of Monterrey.
The company cited numbers from the Federal Commission for Telecommunications.
Homes and businesses in the city were recently balloted on their preferred long distance carrier now that Telefonos de Mexico has lost its long-time monopoly.
Alestra said it had received the 74,435 ballots of the 103,209 who decided to change their service.
Alestra is a joint venture between Mexican conglomerate, financial group VISA-BANCOMER and AT&T.
